name: Can I use my ADU for a home office or guest house instead of a rental?

mainEntity.name: Do ADUs have to be rented out, or can they be designed for family, office, or multigenerational use only?
mainEntity.text: Do ADUs have to be rented out, or can they be designed for family, office, or multigenerational use only?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU is flexible and does not need to be treated as an income property. Many homeowners build one as a family suite, long-term guest house, caregiver space, or private work-from-home studio. The design should match the intended use because a rental-focused layout may prioritize privacy and separate entry, while a family-use unit may prioritize accessibility and connection to the main home. Homeowners should think carefully about bath placement, storage, natural light, noise control, and whether the space should feel fully independent or more integrated with the house. Even if the unit will not be rented, it still needs to meet permit, safety, and habitability standards. The best ADU design is the one that matches the real use case instead of copying a generic rental layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU does not have to be used as a rental. Many homeowners build one for family housing, a guest suite, caregiver space, or a private office and studio, as long as the unit meets habitability and permit requirements.
